title: A Unified Framework for Diffusion Model Unlearning with f-Divergence
claim: A loss family's gradient amplitude varies sharply with its divergence parameter and error magnitude, so the choice of divergence matters.
layout: 2 side-by-side 3D surface panels, left-to-right, each with colorbar and highlighted dashed curve
description: Two side-by-side 3D surface plots, each with a viridis colorbar on the right. The x-axis is MSE, the y-axis is the divergence parameter alpha, and the z-axis is gradient amplitude. The left panel covers alpha from 0 to 1 and MSE from 0 to about 9. The surface forms a smooth hill that peaks near 0.30 at low MSE and slopes down to a flat, dark purple floor at high MSE. A dashed red curve, labeled alpha=0.5 in the legend, runs along the ridge and then down the slope. The right panel covers alpha from 1 to 2 and MSE from 0 to 1. The surface is mostly flat and dark, with a sharp yellow spike up to about 7 near high MSE. A dashed red curve marks alpha=2. The eye goes first to the tall colorful peaks and the red dashed curves.
caption: Gradient amplitude for losses derived from $\alpha$-divergences, varying $\alpha$ and $MSE$. Left: gradient amplitude for $0<\alpha<1$, highlighting the H$^2$ divergence ($\alpha = 0.5$). Right: gradient amplitude for $\alpha>1$, including the $\chi^2$ divergence ($\alpha = 2$).
abstract: Most existing methods for concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models minimize a mean squared error (MSE) loss between the denoiser outputs conditioned on a target and an anchor concept, which is implicitly the KL divergence between two Gaussians. We generalize this objective to any $f$-divergence, recovering MSE as the KL instance, and identify a family of $Î±$-divergences whose Gaussian closed-form yields cheap, MSE-like training objectives. For the remaining $f$-divergences, we provide a min-max objective based on the variational formulation of the $f$-divergence. We theoretically analyze and numerically validate how different $f$-divergences impact the gradient magnitude and the convergence properties of the algorithm, affecting the quality of unlearning. For instance, we observe that the Hellinger closed-form instance consistently dominates MSE across multiple scenarios. More generally, the proposed unified framework offers a flexible paradigm for selecting the optimal divergence based on the application and user goal, allowing for finer control over the trade-off between unlearning efficacy and generative fidelity.
